beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Forty one days ago, the world stopped making sense.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: The power went out. The phones went quiet. And the dead started walking.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Since then, five of us have been hiding at an old gas station on Highway Nine. Mile marker forty one.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: We have one rule. Never go out after dark.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Tonight, we broke it.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Let me back up. This is home.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Two pumps, zero gas, a roof that leaks, and a sign that lost half its letters.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Inside, we've got canned beans, a radio that only plays static, and a cooler full of hope.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: And these are the people I'd die for. Hopefully not today.

card.title: MAGS
card.sub: Mechanic. Fixes anything. Trusts no one.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: That's Mags. She can fix an engine with a paperclip and a bad attitude.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: I heard that, Cole.

card.title: DOOLEY
card.sub: Retired soldier. Never takes his boots off.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Dooley's the oldest. Forty years in the army, and he still sleeps with his boots on.

beats.name: DOOLEY
beats.text: Boots on means you're ready. Boots off means you're dinner.

card.title: PIP
card.sub: Age 12. The brains. Owner of Biscuit.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Pip is twelve. Smartest person here. Don't tell the others.

beats.name: PIP
beats.text: I can hear you too. And Biscuit says hi.

card.title: TANK
card.sub: Biggest guy in the county. Afraid of spiders, dark, and loud noises.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: And that's Tank. Six foot six, three hundred pounds, and scared of literally everything.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Is that a spider? Please tell me that's not a spider.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: It was a raisin.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Every morning starts the same. Mags checks the doors. Dooley checks the road. Pip checks the radio.

beats.name: PIP
beats.text: Still nothing. Just static. Same as yesterday.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: And Tank checks under every table. Twice.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Dinner is the same every night too. Beans. Cold. Out of the can.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: I used to hate beans. Now I dream about beans. Is that weird? That feels weird.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Everything about you is weird, Tank. That's why we keep you.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: And Biscuit? Biscuit eats better than all of us. Nobody knows how. Nobody asks.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: But here's the truth. We're running out. Of food. Of water. Of time.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Every week, there's more of them on the highway. And fewer of us anywhere else.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Forty one days, and we haven't seen another living person. Not one.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Here's how this works. Every like on this episode becomes one supply point for us.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: And the most liked comment decides what we do next. Build walls. Find food. Take in new survivors. Your call.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: But first, we had a problem.

beats.name: DOOLEY
beats.text: It's nothing. Just a tickle.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: That's not a tickle. That cough has been getting worse for three days.

beats.name: PIP
beats.text: He needs medicine. The pharmacy in Bellwood still has some. I saw it on the map.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Bellwood was six miles away. Six miles of road we hadn't walked in weeks.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Six miles? Like, on foot? Through zombie land?

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Unless you've got a car that runs on fear, big guy.

beats.name: DOOLEY
beats.text: I'll go. I'm the one who's sick. I'm not sending kids out for my medicine.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: You can barely walk to the door without coughing, Dooley. You're staying.

beats.name: PIP
beats.text: I'll go! I know the way. I have the map memorized.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Absolutely not, Pip.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: In the end, it was decided. Mags, because she can fix anything we break. Tank, because he can carry anything we find. And me, because somebody has to keep those two from killing each other.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Wait. When did I volunteer? I don't remember volunteering.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Turns out Mags did have a car. Sort of.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: She's ugly, she's loud, and she has exactly one quarter tank. Her name is Doris.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: So that afternoon, Mags, Tank and I loaded up Doris and drove toward Bellwood.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: The highway was a graveyard of cars. Doors open. Bags left behind. Nobody coming back for them.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Okay. Okay. I'm fine. This is fine. Everything is totally fine.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Tank, you're breathing so loud they can hear you in Canada.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Halfway there, we passed a car with a note taped to the windshield.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Went to Bellwood Fire Station. Safe zone. Food and water. Come find us.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: The note was dated three weeks ago. Nobody had come back for that car either.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Mags kept the note. She didn't say anything. She just folded it up and put it in her pocket.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: So, if there's a safe zone with food, why aren't we going there right now?

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Because notes don't come with guarantees, Tank. Three weeks is a long time out here.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Then Doris made a sound no car should ever make.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: No, no, no. Don't you dare quit on me now.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: We were two miles from Bellwood. On foot. With an hour of daylight left.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Bellwood used to be a nice little town. Now it was quiet. Too quiet.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: The pharmacy was right where Pip said it would be. Windows smashed, door hanging open.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: We walked down the middle of Main Street. Past the diner. Past the bank. Past a phone booth with someone still inside it.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Don't look at it. Don't look at it. Why are you looking at it?

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: It's stuck, Tank. It can't open the door. Just keep walking.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Why is it always a creepy door? Why can't it ever be a nice door?

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Inside, the shelves were nearly bare. But Mags found something behind the counter.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Cough syrup. Antibiotics. Bandages. Jackpot.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: That's when we heard it.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: A groan. Low and slow. Coming from the back room.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Please be a cat. Please be a really big cat.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: It was not a cat.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: It was the pharmacist. Still wearing his name tag. Gary.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Hi, Gary. We're just gonna take these and go. Nice and slow.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Gary did not want us to go.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Tank screamed. A sound so high pitched, every dog in Bellwood started barking.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: And then, he did something none of us expected.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: He grabbed a shopping cart, closed his eyes, and charged.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Gary went one way. The cart went the other. Tank ended up in the cough drop aisle.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Tank! That was actually amazing!

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Did I win? I had my eyes closed. Did I win?

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: We grabbed everything we could carry and ran.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: But Tank's scream had done something else. It had rung the dinner bell.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: From every alley and doorway in Bellwood, they started coming.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: We ran two miles back to Doris with half the town behind us.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Get in! Get in! Get in!

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Mags hit the dashboard twice, said a word I can't repeat, and Doris roared back to life.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: We got back to the station just as the sun went down.

beats.name: DOOLEY
beats.text: You're late. And you brought friends.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: They had followed the engine noise. Dozens of them, shuffling up Highway Nine in the dark.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Our barricade was three tables, a vending machine and a lot of duct tape.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: In my defense, I said we needed more duct tape. I said that. Two weeks ago.

beats.name: PIP
beats.text: It's not going to hold. I did the math. It's really not going to hold.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Dooley gave everyone a job.

beats.name: DOOLEY
beats.text: Mags, the back door. Tank, the windows. Pip, the lights. Cole, with me.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Dooley loaded his old shotgun. Two shells. He said that was one more than he'd ever need.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Then the first one hit the glass.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Then another. Then ten more.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: Back door's holding! For now! Somebody tell me the front is holding!

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: The front was not holding.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Biscuit barked at the window. Pip grabbed her and held her mouth shut. Every sound made it worse.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: The vending machine started to slide.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: It's moving! The vending machine is moving! Why is it moving?

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Pip had an idea. A crazy one.

beats.name: PIP
beats.text: They follow noise, right? So let's give them noise. Somewhere else.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: She climbed onto the roof with the old radio, cranked the static all the way up, and threw it as far as she could into the cornfield.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: The radio landed in the field, hissing like a broken TV.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: And one by one, the dead turned around.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Pip. Pip, you're a genius.

beats.name: PIP
beats.text: I know. I'm twelve. I've been saying this.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: We didn't sleep that night. Nobody did. We just sat in the dark and listened to them walk away.

beats.name: DOOLEY
beats.text: Medicine's working. Thank you. All of you.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Day one of the rest of our lives. We made it.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Outside, the static from the field went on all night. A tiny noise, saving five lives.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: In the morning, we counted what we had left. Half a jar of peanut butter. Nine cans of beans. And one very proud twelve year old.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: But we can't do that again. Next time, they won't turn around.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Pip's radio trick worked once. The barricade almost didn't. And Doris is down to her last few drops of gas.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: If we're going to survive the next forty one days, we need more than luck. We need a plan. And we need help.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: So here's where you come in. Every like on this episode is one supply point for Mile Forty One.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: With enough supplies, we can build real walls. Fix the generator. Put up a watchtower. Or go back for more food.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Leave a comment with what we should do next. The most liked comment decides episode two.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: And if you want to join the group, tell us your name and your skill in the comments. The best ones might just show up at our door.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: One more thing.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: That night, the radio inside the station turned on by itself.

beats.name: RADIO
beats.text: Is anyone out there? This is Bellwood Fire Station. We have food. We have water.

beats.name: RADIO
beats.text: But something is coming from the north. Something big. Please, if you can hear this.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Then the radio went dead.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: I'm Cole. This is Mile Forty One. And we're still here. For now.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: Next time on Mile Forty One. We go looking for the voice on the radio.

beats.name: MAGS
beats.text: If that fire station is real, it changes everything.

beats.name: COLE
beats.text: And whatever is coming from the north, it isn't slowing down.

beats.name: TANK
beats.text: Can we vote for the option where nobody goes outside? Is that an option?

card.title: MILE 41
card.sub: Like = 1 supply  ·  Comment = your vote  ·  Subscribe to survive
